events.title: Documentary and Dialogue: ‘College Behind Bars’ Screening #2
events.description: Arapahoe Libraries will host a four-part Documentary and Dialogue series in 2026. These documentary film screenings and facilitated conversations aim to allow guests an opportunity to reflect on their own experiences and learn from the experiences of others. Each conversation is guided by an expert facilitator who will invite us to reflect on the film and dig deeply into the material. The series is designed to spark connection and promote listening and understanding. Join us for part four of the series where we will view College Behind Bars , the inspiring, emotional, deeply human story of men and women struggling to earn college degrees while in prison for serious crimes. Over four years of study, they become scholars, shatter stereotypes, reckon with their pasts and prepare to reenter society. A groundbreaking exploration of incarceration, injustice, race in America and the transformative power of education, from Ken Burns and PBS. Following the documentary, our facilitator will guide a reflective conversation with the audience on the topic. Light snacks will be provided. DISCOVER MORE Join us November 12 for a Featured Artist Reception with Unchained Voices , a Colorado nonprofit amplifying the artwork and stories of people who are incarcerated.

events.title: A Haunted History
events.description: Do you love the supernatural and all things spooky? Is Halloween your favorite holiday? Celebrate the Halloween season with magician and mentalist Erica Sodos. This interactive presentation will blend storytelling, history, humor and astonishing illusions to explore the mysteries of the Victorian Spiritualism era. Together, we’ll delve into spirit communication, tarot, divination and the origins of Halloween in this fun and enchanting program. DISCOVER MORE Join us for these upcoming Halloween events: Friday, October 9: Halloween Tales at Teatime: Adult Storytime Tuesday, October 20: Crows, Crafts & Curiosities Note: This event is intended for adults (ages 18+) based on the topic, material covered, or skills and tools being used. Offering age-appropriate programming allows us to craft memorable and personalized experiences for all our patrons, no matter their age. Manage your event registration through " My Events " when signed in to a library account.

events.title: Open Mic Night
events.description: Join us for an open mic night at Koelbel Library in the Forum Theater! Poetry, music and comedy are all encouraged. Sign up for a five-minute slot upon arrival. Light refreshments will be provided. Please register yourself and guests online to reserve seats in the room.

events.title: Neighborhood Memory Cafe - Colorado Railroad Museum & Galloping Goose
events.description: Do you have a loved one or care for someone with memory loss? This social group is just right for both of you! Get your creative juices flowing with a fun activity to complete together, explore items from the past, or learn about something new. Plus, connect with other families and browse library and community resources. A museum guide will talk about this specialized railcar series developed in the 1930s that ran throughout the Colorado Rockies. They'll also answer questions and bring a trunk of items from the railroad's past for us to explore.

events.title: Clases de Computación para Adultos en Eloise May
events.description: Clases de Computación para Adultos en Eloise May Si no tienes experiencia con las computadoras o no te sientes cómodo(a) usándolas, únete a nuestra clase para aprender a usar tu computadora de una manera muy fácil y comenzando desde cero. Las clases incluyen temas como introducción a la computación, uso de la internet y correo electrónico, como usar ZOOM y como navegar el portal de la escuela de tus hijos. Las personas interesadas, deben registrarse personalmente en la biblioteca Eloise May, antes del 12 de octubre 2026. Cupos limitados. events.title: Fright Night: How to Write Scary Stories
events.description: Spooky season is here! The days are getting shorter, jack-o'-lanterns grin from front porches, and 12-foot skeletons are taking over neighborhoods everywhere. There's no better time to write something that sends a chill down your reader's spine. Join award-winning author and playwright Marty Chan for an interactive workshop on crafting unforgettable scary stories. Through fun writing games, brainstorming exercises, and practical storytelling techniques, you'll learn how to create stories that linger long after the last page. Email addresses are required to receive Zoom information. Have questions about attending an online event? Visit Online Event FAQs . Writing a book? Check out our Writers’ Resources page for free resources on writing, research and formatting and to submit your original work for publishing. events.title: Koelbel Library Volunteer Drop-In for Teens
events.description: Are you a teen in grades 7-12 who needs to earn volunteer hours? Are you looking for a way to have fun while helping out? Check out this opportunity to earn some volunteer hours while supporting library programming and services. We will have a variety of prep work and other activities for teens to help with, including testing crafts! Teens can stay the full time or part of the time, and will earn volunteer credit for the hours they attend the program. If you have any paperwork you need filled out, please bring it with you. If you have other verification needs, please contact us. This volunteer program is for teens in grades 7-12, and will take place at Koelbel Library in Centennial, CO. We are not an approved court ordered volunteer agency and we cannot approve hours for any court ordered service for teens or adults.
